boards.title: 10 Late-Night Runs That Explain Bates College
boards.description: Discover the essential late-night food stops for Bates students, from on-campus staples like the Bobcat Den to local Lewiston favorites that stay open after hours.

cards.title: The Cereal Wall at Commons
cards.subtitle: Late-Night Study Fuel
cards.notes: Visit the massive cereal wall for a late-night snack during extended finals hours or before the doors close at 9:00 PM on weekdays.
cards.short_summary: The central dining hall at Bates, known for its single-hall community and iconic cereal selection.
cards.evidence_claim: The Commons is the primary dining hall where students gather late, featuring a well-known cereal wall and staying open until 9:00 PM Monday-Thursday.
cards.source_title: Hours of Operation and Meal Prices | Dining, Conferences and Campus Events (DCCE)
cards.access_notes: Open until 9:00 PM Monday through Thursday; hours vary on weekends and during breaks.

cards.title: Late Night at the Den
cards.subtitle: Chase Hall Social Hub
cards.notes: Order a Bates Burger or mozzarella sticks during designated late-night hours, typically on Wednesday nights until 11:00 PM.
cards.short_summary: A retail dining space in Chase Hall that serves as a popular alternative to the main dining hall.
cards.evidence_claim: The Bobcat Den reopened for late-night hours on Wednesday nights until 11:00 PM to provide a mid-week social dining option.
cards.source_title: First Time in Four Years: Den Opens For Late-Night Option - The Bates Student
cards.access_notes: Late-night hours are currently limited to Wednesdays until 11:00 PM; check campus signage for seasonal updates.

cards.title: Kim's Kitchen
cards.subtitle: The Closest Off-Campus Run
cards.notes: Walk across Russell Street for fried rice or fries at this family-run convenience store, a staple for students living in nearby dorms.
cards.short_summary: A neighborhood variety store and kitchen located directly across from the Bates campus.
cards.evidence_claim: Kim's Kitchen is a frequent late-night destination for Bates students, located on the corner of Bardwell and Russell Streets.
cards.source_title: More than just a Convenience Store: Meet the Owner of Kim's Kitchen - The Bates Student
cards.access_notes: Located at 88 Russell St; typically open until 10:00 PM or 11:00 PM on weekends.

cards.title: Lewiston House of Pizza
cards.subtitle: Midnight Pizza Delivery
cards.notes: Order a late-night pie or Greek specialty; they stay open until midnight on Friday and Saturday for delivery or pickup.
cards.short_summary: A long-standing local pizzeria known for Greek-style pizza and late weekend hours.
cards.evidence_claim: Lewiston House of Pizza is open until 12:00 AM on Friday and Saturday nights.
cards.source_title: Lewiston House of Pizza Lewiston Maine Restaurant Menu - MenusInLA
cards.access_notes: Open until 12:00 AM on Friday and Saturday; closes at 10:00 PM on other nights.

cards.title: Sam's on Sabattus
cards.subtitle: Maine Italian Tradition
cards.notes: Grab a signature Maine Italian sandwich on a fresh-baked roll; the Sabattus Street location is open until midnight on weekends.
cards.short_summary: A regional chain famous for its specific style of Italian sandwiches and fresh rolls.
cards.evidence_claim: The Sam's Italian Foods location at 963 Sabattus St is open until 12:00 AM on Friday and Saturday.
cards.source_title: Contact — Sam's Italian Foods
cards.access_notes: Open until 12:00 AM on Friday and Saturday; 11:00 PM on Thursdays.

cards.title: The 24/7 Main Street Run
cards.subtitle: Always Open Convenience
cards.notes: Head to Main Street for 24-hour access to snacks, drinks, and quick bites when everything else in town is closed.
cards.short_summary: A 24-hour convenience store located a short distance from the campus perimeter.
cards.evidence_claim: The 7-Eleven at 345 Main St in Lewiston is open 24 hours a day, 7 days a week.
cards.source_title: 345 Main St Lewiston ME 04240-7028 - 7-Eleven
cards.access_notes: Open 24/7 for walk-in service.

cards.title: Dunkin' on Main
cards.subtitle: Late Coffee & Donuts
cards.notes: Fuel up with coffee or donuts until 9:00 PM at this Main Street location, a common stop for students heading back to campus.
cards.short_summary: A popular coffee and donut chain with multiple locations in Lewiston.
cards.evidence_claim: The Dunkin' at 420 Main St is open until 9:00 PM daily.
cards.source_title: Dunkin' locations in Lewiston
cards.access_notes: Open daily until 9:00 PM.

cards.title: DaVinci's in the Mill
cards.subtitle: Late Weekend Italian
cards.notes: Enjoy brick-oven pizza or garlic knots in the historic Bates Mill complex; they serve until 10:00 PM on Friday and Saturday.
cards.short_summary: An Italian restaurant located in a refurbished textile mill, popular for its atmosphere and food.
cards.evidence_claim: DaVinci's Italian Eatery is open until 10:00 PM on Friday and Saturday nights.
cards.source_title: Reservations - DaVinci's Italian Eatery | Lewiston, Maine
cards.access_notes: Open until 10:00 PM on Friday and Saturday; 9:00 PM on other nights.

cards.title: Governor's Late Night
cards.subtitle: Classic Maine Comfort
cards.notes: Visit for a late-night dessert or burger; this Maine staple is open until 9:00 PM on weekends for a sit-down meal.
cards.short_summary: A family-style restaurant and bakery known for its desserts and Maine-centric menu.
cards.evidence_claim: Governor's Restaurant in Lewiston is open until 9:00 PM on Friday and Saturday.
cards.source_title: Locations - Governor's Restaurant & Bakery
cards.access_notes: Open until 9:00 PM on Friday and Saturday; 8:00 PM on other days.

cards.title: Forage Market
cards.subtitle: Early Morning Recovery
cards.notes: While not open late at night, Forage is the go-to morning-after spot for wood-fired bagels starting at 8:00 AM.
cards.short_summary: A popular downtown market and bakery famous for its hand-rolled, wood-fired bagels.
cards.evidence_claim: Forage Market is a central part of the Bates student food culture, opening at 8:00 AM daily for breakfast.
cards.source_title: Forage Market - Lewiston
cards.access_notes: Open daily from 8:00 AM to 1:00 PM.

boards.title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
boards.description: Discover the specific study nooks, social lounges, and quiet retreats that define the daily student experience at Bates College beyond the standard tour stops.

cards.title: The Glass-Walled Perry Atrium
cards.subtitle: Pettengill Hall
cards.notes: Study among indoor trees and a waterfall fountain. This three-story glass space offers views of Lake Andrews and is furnished with elegant Thomas Moser wood furniture.
cards.short_summary: A light-filled three-story atrium in Pettengill Hall featuring indoor nature and premium wood furniture for quiet study.
cards.evidence_claim: The Perry Atrium in Pettengill Hall features indoor trees, a waterfall fountain, and Thomas Moser furniture, serving as a favorite spot for quiet study.
cards.source_title: Pettengill Hall | Campus Tour - Bates College
cards.access_notes: Open during academic building hours; typically accessible until late evening for students with ID.

cards.title: The Mezzanine Dining Retreat
cards.subtitle: The Commons, Second Level
cards.notes: Escape the main dining hall's bustle on the second level. It offers a quieter atmosphere for meals and informal conversations with a view of the servery below.
cards.short_summary: A quieter, elevated dining area within the main Commons building preferred by students for focused conversation.
cards.evidence_claim: The Commons mezzanine provides a smaller and quieter dining space compared to the large main dining area.
cards.source_title: Commons | Campus Tour - Bates College
cards.access_notes: Accessible during standard dining hours; requires a meal plan or payment for entry to the building.

cards.title: The Little Room Social Hub
cards.subtitle: Chase Hall, Ground Floor
cards.notes: Head to the ground floor for billiards, table tennis, and arcade games. This multi-room social space is a primary destination for late-night student recreation.
cards.short_summary: A multi-room recreation space in Chase Hall equipped with various table games and social lounge areas.
cards.evidence_claim: The Little Room on the ground floor of Chase Hall includes billiards, table tennis, foosball, and air hockey for student use.
cards.source_title: Student Spaces on Campus | Campus Life - Bates College
cards.access_notes: Open daily during Chase Hall building hours; free for student use.

cards.title: The Collaborative Ground Floor
cards.subtitle: George and Helen Ladd Library
cards.notes: Choose this level for group projects and active discussion. It is the designated loud floor and houses the Math & Stats Workshop for peer tutoring.
cards.short_summary: The designated floor for group work and collaborative study within the main campus library.
cards.evidence_claim: The ground floor of Ladd Library is where students work together in groups and is home to the Math & Stats workshop.
cards.source_title: A Guide to Study Spots at Bates - The Bates Student
cards.access_notes: Open late during the semester; Bates ID required for entry during late-night hours.

cards.title: The Olin Music Practice Rooms
cards.subtitle: Olin Arts Center
cards.notes: Find focus in one of ten soundproof practice rooms equipped with pianos. These spaces are open to all students, not just music majors, for practice or quiet work.
cards.short_summary: Soundproof individual and group practice rooms in the Olin Arts Center available for student musical practice.
cards.evidence_claim: The Olin Arts Center houses ten practice rooms with pianos and individual/group practice rooms used by the Department of Music and open to non-majors.
cards.source_title: Olin Arts Center | Music - Bates College
cards.access_notes: Accessible during Olin Arts Center building hours; rooms are typically first-come, first-served.

cards.title: The Hedge Hall Study Lounges
cards.subtitle: Hedge Hall
cards.notes: Utilize the lounge areas on the upper floors of this renovated former lab. They are convenient spots for daytime work between classes in Philosophy or Environmental Studies.
cards.short_summary: Modern lounge spaces in Hedge Hall providing quiet areas for independent study during the academic day.
cards.evidence_claim: Hedge Hall contains numerous lounge areas that serve as convenient spots for students to work during the day.
cards.source_title: A Guide to Study Spots at Bates - The Bates Student
cards.access_notes: Open during academic building hours; typically 8:00 AM to late evening.

cards.title: Global Education Lounges
cards.subtitle: Roger Williams Hall
cards.notes: Secure a spot in these popular lounges early in the evening. Located near the Center for Global Education, they offer a quiet environment with few distractions.
cards.short_summary: Quiet study lounges located in Roger Williams Hall, often used by students studying languages and global cultures.
cards.evidence_claim: Roger Williams Hall features lounges that are popular for getting work done with few distractions, though they fill up early in the evening.
cards.source_title: A Guide to Study Spots at Bates - The Bates Student
cards.access_notes: Accessible during academic building hours; student ID may be required for after-hours access.

cards.title: The Sanctuary of Gomes Chapel
cards.subtitle: Gomes Chapel
cards.notes: Visit for moments of solitude and serenity. The nondenominational space features banners of world faith traditions and is open to all for quiet reflection.
cards.short_summary: A historic, nondenominational chapel providing a quiet space for reflection and multifaith community activities.
cards.evidence_claim: Gomes Chapel is a place of solitude and serenity open to all students for religious practice or quiet reflection.
cards.source_title: The Peter J. Gomes Chapel | Multifaith Chaplaincy - Bates College
cards.access_notes: Open daily for student use; hours may vary based on scheduled services or events.

cards.title: The Lakeside Amphitheater
cards.subtitle: Lake Andrews
cards.notes: Gather at this granite amphitheater on the shores of 'The Puddle.' It is a primary spot for outdoor relaxation, wildlife watching, and seasonal student events.
cards.short_summary: A granite outdoor amphitheater on the edge of Lake Andrews used for student gatherings and relaxation.
cards.evidence_claim: The Florence Keigwin Amphitheater near the Olin Arts Center is a popular spot for students to hang out by Lake Andrews.
cards.source_title: Lake Andrews | Campus Tour - Bates College
cards.access_notes: Outdoor public space accessible 24/7; best used during daylight hours.

cards.title: The Chase Hall MakerSpace
cards.subtitle: Chase Hall, Room 161
cards.notes: Access 3D printers, sewing machines, and art supplies in this creative community space. It is tucked away behind the SCBC kitchen for student projects.
cards.short_summary: A student-led creative space in Chase Hall providing tools for arts, crafts, and technical projects.
cards.evidence_claim: The MakerSpace in Chase Hall 161 offers 3D printers, sewing machines, and basic art supplies for communal student use.
cards.source_title: Student Spaces on Campus | Campus Life - Bates College
cards.access_notes: Open during Chase Hall building hours; some equipment may require coordination with Campus Life staff.

boards.title: Zero Dollars: 10 Hangs That Cost Nothing
boards.description: Discover free social spaces, cultural venues, and natural retreats at Bates College that require no admission or purchase for students and visitors.

cards.title: Bates College Museum of Art
cards.subtitle: Olin Arts Center
cards.notes: Explore contemporary and modern art exhibitions at no cost. The museum is open to the public and serves as a major cultural hub on the edge of Lake Andrews.
cards.short_summary: A teaching museum offering free admission to all visitors to view its permanent collections and rotating exhibitions.
cards.evidence_claim: The public is welcome to view our exhibitions, free of charge. Admission Information: Free admission.
cards.source_title: Visit | Museum of Art | Bates College
cards.access_notes: Open Monday-Saturday 10 AM – 5 PM (with extended hours until 7:30 PM on Mondays and Wednesdays during the academic year).

cards.title: Hiking Mount David
cards.subtitle: Mountain Avenue
cards.notes: Climb this 381-foot rocky outcrop for panoramic views of Lewiston and the campus. It is a popular spot for watching sunrises and stargazing with friends.
cards.short_summary: A short, five-minute hike to a secluded hilltop offering scenic views of the surrounding Maine countryside.
cards.evidence_claim: Mount David is a small hill next to campus... Trails maintained by students lead to a rocky summit with great views. This private property is a popular destination.
cards.source_title: Mount David | Campus Tour - Bates College
cards.access_notes: Accessible via trails off Mountain Avenue; open to the Bates community and respectful visitors.

cards.title: Lake Andrews
cards.subtitle: The Puddle
cards.notes: Walk the lakeside path or sit at the granite amphitheater. Four laps around the water equal one mile, making it a favorite for casual exercise and relaxation.
cards.short_summary: A central campus pond featuring a walking path and the Florence Keigwin Amphitheater for outdoor gathering.
cards.evidence_claim: A typical day finds walkers doing circuits on the lakeside path (four times around is about a mile) as students hang out at the granite amphitheater.
cards.source_title: Lake Andrews | Campus Tour - Bates College
cards.access_notes: Publicly accessible outdoor space; visitors are asked to respect shoreline vegetation and nesting ducks.

cards.title: Music Department Concerts
cards.subtitle: 75 Russell Street
cards.notes: Attend student and faculty musical performances throughout the semester. Most concerts held in this hall are open to the public without a ticket fee.
cards.short_summary: Free musical performances hosted by the Bates Music Department in the Olin Arts Center.
cards.evidence_claim: All Concerts will be held in the Olin Arts Center Concert Hall and are free of charge unless otherwise stated.
cards.source_title: Public Art Events | The Arts - Bates College
cards.access_notes: Check the online arts calendar for specific event dates and times; most are free and open to the public.

cards.title: The Little Room
cards.subtitle: Chase Hall Ground Floor
cards.notes: Play billiards, ping-pong, or foosball in this multi-room social space. It is a dedicated area for students to relax and engage in casual gaming.
cards.short_summary: A student social space in Chase Hall equipped with various table games and a karaoke area.
cards.evidence_claim: The “Little Room” is located on the ground floor of Chase hall... Included in this space: Billiards Table; Table Tennis/Ping-Pong Table; Foosball Table; Air Hockey Table.
cards.source_title: Student Spaces on Campus | Campus Life - Bates College
cards.access_notes: Open to all Bates students on a first-come, first-served basis.

cards.title: Peter J. Gomes Chapel
cards.subtitle: 275 College Street
cards.notes: Visit this historic Gothic-style chapel for quiet reflection or to attend multifaith events. It serves as a peaceful sanctuary for the entire campus community.
cards.short_summary: A nondenominational chapel providing a space for solitude, serenity, and inclusive community gatherings.
cards.evidence_claim: Open to all, Gomes Chapel is a place of solitude, serenity, and community... Inside, banners of the world's major faith traditions offer reminders of Bates' inclusive founding.
cards.source_title: Gomes Chapel | Campus Tour - Bates College
cards.access_notes: Open for access with a Bates ID; public access is available during scheduled events.

cards.title: Thorncrag Nature Sanctuary
cards.subtitle: Montello Street
cards.notes: Hike over four miles of trails in this 450-acre preserve. It is the highest point in Lewiston and offers birdwatching and winter sledding opportunities.
cards.short_summary: A large wildlife preserve and bird sanctuary with extensive hiking trails and scenic overlooks.
cards.evidence_claim: Thorncrag Sanctuary is a 450 acre nature preserve... Fees: No. Passive recreation... is actively encouraged.
cards.source_title: Thorncrag Sanctuary - Stanton Bird Club
cards.access_notes: Open daily from sunrise to sunset. Dogs and bicycles are not permitted.

cards.title: Muskie Archives & Special Collections
cards.subtitle: 70 Campus Avenue
cards.notes: Browse rare books and historical records of the college. The archives are open for research and often feature exhibits on local and institutional history.
cards.short_summary: The college's repository for historically significant records, rare books, and the papers of Senator Edmund S. Muskie.
cards.evidence_claim: The library serves a broad and diverse audience by producing exhibits, conducting educational and outreach programs... Walk-in, in-building use... available for those doing research.
cards.source_title: Archives | Bates College
cards.access_notes: Research hours are typically Monday-Friday; appointments are recommended for specific collection access.

cards.title: Ladd Library
cards.subtitle: 48 Campus Avenue
cards.notes: Utilize the open shelves and study spaces in the main campus library. It is a central hub for academic work and quiet group meetings.
cards.short_summary: The primary academic library at Bates, offering extensive collections and diverse study environments.
cards.evidence_claim: Items on open shelves are available for anyone to use in the library... Ladd Library is open to the Bates community via card access.
cards.source_title: Access and Borrowing | Library - Bates College
cards.access_notes: Card access required for entry; open late during the academic semester.

cards.title: Mount David Summit
cards.subtitle: Pettengill Hall
cards.notes: Attend this annual celebration of student research and creative work. It is free and open to the public, showcasing posters, talks, and performances.
cards.short_summary: An annual campus-wide symposium highlighting undergraduate research and artistic achievement.
cards.evidence_claim: The Mount David Summit is Bates' annual campus-wide celebration of student academic achievement... Events are... open to the Bates community as well as the general public.
cards.source_title: Mount David Summit - Bates College
cards.access_notes: Held annually in April; check the college calendar for the specific Friday date.

boards.title: Claimed by 9am: 10 Study Spots Worth Showing Up Early For
boards.description: From the quiet stacks of Ladd Library to the sun-drenched Perry Atrium, Bates College offers a variety of environments for focused academic work and collaborative projects.

cards.title: Ladd Library Third Floor
cards.subtitle: Quiet Individual Study
cards.notes: Head to the third floor for the most silent environment in the library. It features individual carrels and the reservable Salter Room for focused thesis work.
cards.short_summary: The quietest floor of the main campus library, ideal for deep concentration and independent research.
cards.evidence_claim: The third floor of Ladd Library is described as a quiet environment with plenty of seating options, including private study space and the reservable Salter Room.
cards.source_title: Library's Group Study Rooms - Bates College
cards.access_notes: Open to students with Bates ID; hours vary by semester but typically include late night access until midnight or 2am.

cards.title: Perry Atrium
cards.subtitle: Sunlit Social Study
cards.notes: Enjoy views of Lake Andrews through the three-story glass wall. This 8,000-square-foot space features Thomas Moser furniture and a soothing waterfall fountain.
cards.short_summary: A massive, glass-walled atrium in Pettengill Hall known for its natural light and views of 'The Puddle.'
cards.evidence_claim: Perry Atrium is an 8,000-square-foot three-story glass atrium in Pettengill Hall overlooking Lake Andrews, featuring Thomas Moser furniture and a waterfall fountain.
cards.source_title: Pettengill Hall | Campus Tour - Bates College
cards.access_notes: Accessible during building hours; Pettengill Hall typically closes to students at 2am.

cards.title: Bonney Science Center Lounges
cards.subtitle: Modern Collaborative Space
cards.notes: Utilize the newest building on campus for its modern lounges and 'science on display' design. Great for group work between STEM labs.
cards.short_summary: Bates' newest academic building offering contemporary study lounges and collaborative spaces for all students.
cards.evidence_claim: The Bonney Science Center is a community hub with classrooms and study space for all to use, featuring teaching spaces and research labs.
cards.source_title: Bonney Science Center | Campus Tour - Bates College
cards.access_notes: Open to students with Bates ID during building hours.

cards.title: Commons Mezzanine
cards.subtitle: Dining Hall Study
cards.notes: Find a quieter spot for a working lunch on the mezzanine level of the dining hall. It offers a more secluded feel than the main floor.
cards.short_summary: The upper level of the central dining hall, providing a quieter alternative for students who like to study while they eat.
cards.evidence_claim: Commons offers dining spaces including a smaller and quieter mezzanine level and a Fireplace Lounge on the second level.
cards.source_title: Commons | Campus Tour - Bates College
cards.access_notes: Accessible during dining hall operating hours; requires meal plan or payment for entry.

cards.title: Gomes Chapel
cards.subtitle: Contemplative Quiet
cards.notes: Visit for absolute silence and architectural beauty. Meditation cushions are available in the front pews for quiet reflection or reading.
cards.short_summary: A historic Gothic chapel providing a serene and silent environment for contemplation and quiet study.
cards.evidence_claim: The Peter J. Gomes Chapel is open daily from 7 a.m. to 7 p.m. for contemplation and reflection, with meditation cushions in the front pews.
cards.source_title: Quiet Places On Campus | Multifaith Chaplaincy - Bates College
cards.access_notes: Open daily 7am-11pm for Bates ID holders; community access by appointment.

cards.title: Chase Hall Student Lounge
cards.subtitle: Central Student Hub
cards.notes: Located on the ground floor (G02), this lounge serves as a popular social and study space near the 'Little Room' gaming area.
cards.short_summary: A versatile student lounge in the historic Chase Hall, ideal for casual studying and meeting friends.
cards.evidence_claim: The Campus Life Student Lounge (G02) in Chase Hall is a popular social and study space for students.
cards.source_title: Student Spaces on Campus | Campus Life - Bates College
cards.access_notes: Accessible during Chase Hall building hours.

cards.title: Hedge Hall Lounges
cards.subtitle: Humanities Study Nooks
cards.notes: Find cozy lounge areas on the upper floors or use the basement computer lab. These spots are convenient for students in the humanities.
cards.short_summary: Quiet lounges and a computer lab located within the renovated Hedge Hall, home to several academic departments.
cards.evidence_claim: Hedge Hall has numerous classrooms and lounge areas (Hedge 105, 303, 304, G16) available for student use.
cards.source_title: Student Spaces on Campus | Campus Life - Bates College
cards.access_notes: Open during academic building hours for student use.

cards.title: Roger Williams Hall Lounges
cards.subtitle: Global Education Hub
cards.notes: Study in the lounges of this award-winning renovated building. It's a quiet spot for language students and those planning off-campus study.
cards.short_summary: Quiet study lounges located in the building that houses foreign languages and the Center for Global Education.
cards.evidence_claim: Roger Williams Hall features several common area study spaces (G02, H206, H225, H306, H404) available to students.
cards.source_title: Student Spaces on Campus | Campus Life - Bates College
cards.access_notes: Accessible during building hours; lounges often fill up early in the evening.

cards.title: Muskie Archives Upstairs
cards.subtitle: Historic Event Space
cards.notes: When not in use for events, the upstairs area offers comfy furniture and a large, quiet space for studying among college history.
cards.short_summary: A large, quiet upstairs room in the Muskie Archives building, featuring comfortable seating and a scholarly atmosphere.
cards.evidence_claim: The upstairs of the Muskie Archives hosts a large event space with comfy furniture that can hold approximately 120 people.
cards.source_title: Muskie Archives | Campus Events, Conferences & Summer Programs - Bates College
cards.access_notes: Open during archive hours; check for scheduled events which may close the space.

cards.title: Olin Arts Center Room 128
cards.subtitle: Arts-Focused Study
cards.notes: Use this designated classroom space for studying outside of academic hours. It's a great alternative for those near the arts quad.
cards.short_summary: A classroom in the Olin Arts Center specifically identified as available for student study outside of scheduled classes.
cards.evidence_claim: Olin Arts Center Room 128 is listed as a classroom study space available to students for studying outside of academic use.
cards.source_title: Student Spaces on Campus | Campus Life - Bates College
cards.access_notes: Available for study when classes are not in session during building hours.

boards.title: 10 Blocks Off Campus, One Reason Each
boards.description: Explore the essential streets and corridors surrounding Bates College, from historic mill districts to student-favorite dining strips in Lewiston.

cards.title: The Downtown Dining Strip
cards.subtitle: Lisbon Street Corridor
cards.notes: Walk down this historic corridor to find student favorites like Forage Market for bagels and Mother India for authentic North Indian cuisine.
cards.short_summary: A central downtown street known for its diverse culinary scene and historic architecture.
cards.evidence_claim: Lisbon Street is popular with Bates students for its variety of restaurants, including Forage Market and Mother India.
cards.source_title: What to Do in the Lew - The Bates Student
cards.access_notes: Public street accessible 24/7; individual business hours vary.

cards.title: The Boba and Pizza Hub
cards.subtitle: College Street Corridor
cards.notes: Just a 10-minute walk from campus, this block features Tina Thai Express and Pure Thai, both popular for their bubble tea options.
cards.short_summary: A primary thoroughfare connecting the campus to downtown, lined with quick-service student eateries.
cards.evidence_claim: Tina Thai Express and Pure Thai on College Street are noted student destinations for boba and Thai food.
cards.source_title: What to Do in the Lew - The Bates Student
cards.access_notes: Public street; restaurants typically open for lunch and dinner.

cards.title: The Student Supply Run
cards.subtitle: Sabattus Street Corridor
cards.notes: Head here for essential errands at Hannaford or Walgreens, and grab a quick bite at local favorites like Bua Thai.
cards.short_summary: A major commercial corridor providing essential services and grocery options near the college.
cards.evidence_claim: Sabattus Street hosts key student resources like Hannaford, Walgreens, and Bua Thai & Sushi.
cards.source_title: Local Businesses | Parents and Families - Bates College
cards.access_notes: Public commercial corridor; grocery and pharmacy hours vary.

cards.title: The Historic Mill District
cards.subtitle: Lincoln Street Corridor
cards.notes: Visit the renovated Bates Mill complex to dine at Fish Bones American Grill or explore the city's industrial heritage.
cards.short_summary: A riverside street defined by massive 19th-century brick mills now housing offices and restaurants.
cards.evidence_claim: Fish Bones American Grill is located in a historic canal-side mill building on Lincoln Street.
cards.source_title: Fish Bones Grill | Casual Upscale Dining | Lewiston, Maine
cards.access_notes: Public street; mill complex accessible during business hours.

cards.title: The Industrial Waterway
cards.subtitle: Canal Street Corridor
cards.notes: Walk along the canal to see the engineering that powered Lewiston's mills and visit the Maine MILL museum for local history.
cards.short_summary: A street running parallel to the canal system, central to the city's textile manufacturing history.
cards.evidence_claim: The Maine MILL museum is located near Canal Street and offers tours of the historic mill area.
cards.source_title: Plan Your Visit - Maine MILL
cards.access_notes: Public street; museum open Wednesday-Sunday 10am-4pm.

cards.title: The Kennedy Park Gateway
cards.subtitle: Park Street Corridor
cards.notes: This street borders Kennedy Park, a 9-acre green space that hosts community events and the local Art Walk L/A.
cards.short_summary: A downtown street providing access to the city's primary public park and cultural events.
cards.evidence_claim: Kennedy Park is located at 120 Park Street and is a site for community gatherings and music series.
cards.source_title: Facilities • Kennedy Park - Lewiston, Maine
cards.access_notes: Public street and park; park typically open dawn to dusk.

cards.title: The Courthouse Plaza Block
cards.subtitle: Main Street Corridor
cards.notes: Visit the courthouse plaza for community performances or stop by local institutions like Simone's Hot Dog Stand.
cards.short_summary: A major artery featuring civic buildings, local eateries, and public gathering spaces.
cards.evidence_claim: Bates students gather at the courthouse plaza on Main Street for events like acapella performances.
cards.source_title: Lewiston & Maine | Admission - Bates College
cards.access_notes: Public street; plaza is an open public space.

cards.title: The Athletic Corridor
cards.subtitle: Russell Street Corridor
cards.notes: Bordering the north side of campus, this street leads to the Russell Street Track and the Bates Museum of Art.
cards.short_summary: A key campus-adjacent street housing major athletic facilities and the college's art museum.
cards.evidence_claim: The Russell Street Track and Field and the Bates Museum of Art are located along this corridor.
cards.source_title: Russell Street Track and Field - Bates College Athletics
cards.access_notes: Public street; museum and athletic facility hours vary.

cards.title: The Somali Block
cards.subtitle: Pine Street Corridor
cards.notes: Explore the vibrant Somali-owned businesses and markets that have revitalized this downtown neighborhood.
cards.short_summary: A culturally rich street known for its immigrant-owned shops and community resilience.
cards.evidence_claim: Bates students often visit the 'Somali block' on Pine Street to explore local stores and businesses.
cards.source_title: Here's what new Bates students say about Lewiston | News
cards.access_notes: Public street; business hours vary by establishment.

cards.title: The Historic House Row
cards.subtitle: Frye Street Corridor
cards.notes: Walk past these beautiful Victorian houses that serve as Bates student residences and lead to the base of Mount David.
cards.short_summary: A picturesque residential street adjacent to campus featuring historic architecture and trail access.
cards.evidence_claim: Frye Street is home to several Bates student houses and provides access to the Mount David overlook.
cards.source_title: What to Do in the Lew - The Bates Student
cards.access_notes: Public street; residential area.

boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: Discover the unique rituals and long-standing traditions that define the student experience at Bates College, from icy plunges to historic masonry.

cards.title: The Puddle Jump
cards.subtitle: A Mid-Winter Polar Plunge
cards.notes: Join hundreds of students in late winter to jump through a hole cut in the ice of Lake Andrews, a tradition started in 1975 to celebrate the end of a hard Maine winter.
cards.short_summary: An annual winter tradition where students jump into the icy waters of Lake Andrews.
cards.evidence_claim: The Puddle Jump began in 1975 when students cut a hole in the ice on Lake Andrews for a St. Patrick's Day dip; it now features a 'Dip Master' and an official ax.
cards.source_title: Puddle Jump | 150 Years - Bates College
cards.access_notes: Occurs annually during Winter Carnival; open to all students to watch or participate.

cards.title: Ivy Stones
cards.subtitle: Class Year Masonry
cards.notes: Look for engraved granite plaques set into the brickwork of campus buildings; each graduating class since 1879 has designed and installed a unique stone to mark their legacy.
cards.short_summary: A tradition of installing custom-designed class year plaques into campus buildings.
cards.evidence_claim: Since the 1870s, engraved plaques known as ivy stones have been installed in Bates campus buildings to honor each graduating class, with the first placed in 1878.
cards.source_title: Bates ivy stones from 1879 to today | Campus Tour
cards.access_notes: Stones are visible year-round on the exterior of various campus buildings.

cards.title: Winter Carnival Torch Relay
cards.subtitle: Governor-Lit Tradition
cards.notes: Watch the arrival of the carnival torch, traditionally lit by the Governor of Maine and relayed by students from the state capital in Augusta to the Lewiston campus.
cards.short_summary: A torch relay from Augusta to campus that kicks off the annual Winter Carnival.
cards.evidence_claim: The torch relay tradition began in 1958 when Governor Edmund Muskie lit a torch that students relayed from Augusta to campus for the Winter Carnival opening parade.
cards.source_title: January 1958: The Winter Carnival torch tradition | 150 Years | Bates College
cards.access_notes: The relay occurs annually in late January or early February during Winter Carnival.

cards.title: Harvest Dinner
cards.subtitle: A Campus-Wide Feast
cards.notes: Experience the annual themed Thanksgiving-style feast at Commons, featuring elaborate ice sculptures and a menu of regional favorites like Italian pudding.
cards.short_summary: An elaborate annual themed dinner hosted by Dining Services for the entire community.
cards.evidence_claim: The Harvest Dinner is a 40-year-old tradition hosted by Commons around November 19th, featuring ice sculptures and a themed buffet.
cards.source_title: Let's Get Traditional: The Best Bates Traditions - The Bates Student
cards.access_notes: Held annually in November; requires a meal plan or guest pass for entry.

cards.title: Commencement Sunrise Climb
cards.subtitle: Senior Class Farewell
cards.notes: Climb the rocky summit of Mount David on the morning of Commencement to watch the sunrise with fellow graduates, a final reflective moment before the ceremony.
cards.short_summary: A tradition where graduating seniors climb Mount David to watch the sunrise together.
cards.evidence_claim: Graduating seniors climb Mount David on the night before Commencement to watch the morning sunrise together as a class tradition.
cards.source_title: Mount David | Campus Tour - Bates College
cards.access_notes: Accessible via trails off Mountain Avenue; the sunrise climb is specific to Commencement morning.

cards.title: Village Club Series (VCS)
cards.subtitle: Thursday Night Coffeehouse
cards.notes: Attend this student-run performance series every Thursday night for live music and a coffeehouse atmosphere in the Benjamin Mays Center.
cards.short_summary: A long-running weekly performance series featuring student and guest artists.
cards.evidence_claim: The Village Club Series (VCS) has been a Bates institution since 1993, held most Thursdays at 8:00pm in the Benjamin Mays Center.
cards.source_title: Village Club Series | Campus Life - Bates College
cards.access_notes: Events typically start at 8:00 PM on Thursdays during the academic year.

cards.title: Lick-It Dance
cards.subtitle: Queer-Centric Celebration
cards.notes: Participate in this high-energy, costume-heavy dance hosted by OutFront, traditionally held in the Gray Cage as a celebration of queer identity and expression.
cards.short_summary: An annual inclusive dance event focused on queer community and creative costumes.
cards.evidence_claim: Lick-It is an annual dance event hosted by the student group OutFront, known for its expressive costumes and focus on queer identity.
cards.source_title: Important Information for Attendees of Lick-It 2026 | Campus Life | Bates College
cards.access_notes: Held annually in March; open to Bates students and registered guests.

cards.title: The Napkin Board
cards.subtitle: Dining Hall Feedback Loop
cards.notes: Read the physical or digital board in Commons where students post questions on napkins and receive direct, often humorous, responses from Dining Services staff.
cards.short_summary: A unique communication tradition between students and dining staff via napkins.
cards.evidence_claim: The Napkin Board in Commons allows students to communicate with Dining Services; it has both a physical presence and an online version.
cards.source_title: Online Napkin Board | Dining, Conferences and Campus Events (DCCE) - Bates College
cards.access_notes: Accessible during Commons operating hours; digital version available online.

cards.title: The 80s Dance
cards.subtitle: Neon Nostalgia
cards.notes: Don your best neon spandex and vintage gear for the first major social event of the year, featuring 1980s hits and a massive outdoor dance floor on the Library Quad.
cards.short_summary: A massive outdoor dance party themed to the 1980s held early in the fall semester.
cards.evidence_claim: The 80s Dance is described as the first big social event of the year at Bates, typically held on the Library Quad with pizza and 80s music.
cards.source_title: Definitive Ranking of Bates Dances So Far - Her Campus
cards.access_notes: Held annually in the fall; open to the Bates student community.

cards.title: Dinger Day
cards.subtitle: Short Term Softball
cards.notes: Compete in or watch the campus-wide softball tournament held during the final week of Short Term, a high-energy athletic tradition that marks the end of the academic year.
cards.short_summary: A competitive campus-wide softball tournament held during the spring Short Term.
cards.evidence_claim: Dinger Day is a relatively new tradition involving a campus-wide softball tournament held on the last Saturday of Short Term.
cards.source_title: Let's Get Traditional: The Best Bates Traditions - The Bates Student
cards.access_notes: Occurs annually in late May during the final week of Short Term.

boards.title: Your First Weekend at Bates College, Shared as Cards
boards.description: Build a plausible under-21-safe first-weekend sequence, not a ranking. Give each card one role in the sequence and use evergreen places or recurring behaviors rather than one-time events. Be conservative about hours, access, and travel time unless directly sourced.

cards.title: Arrival and Move-In
cards.subtitle: Thursday Morning Kickoff
cards.notes: Arrive at your assigned residence hall to meet your Junior Advisors and Residence Coordinators. Most first-year students move in on the Thursday before classes begin.
cards.short_summary: The official start of the Bates experience begins with move-in day for the incoming class.
cards.evidence_claim: Arrival day for most new students is Thursday, August 27, 2026, as part of the First-Year Experience and New Student Orientation.
cards.source_title: First-Year Orientation Schedule - Bates College
cards.access_notes: Access is restricted to incoming students and their families during designated move-in windows.

cards.title: Opening Convocation
cards.subtitle: Formal Academic Welcome
cards.notes: Process across the Historic Quad to Coram Library for the official welcome ceremony. This tradition marks the formal start of your academic journey at Bates.
cards.short_summary: A century-old tradition where the incoming class is formally welcomed to the Bates community on the Historic Quad.
cards.evidence_claim: Opening Convocation is held annually on the terrace of Coram Library, featuring an academic procession across the Historic Quad.
cards.source_title: Opening Convocation at Bates offers timeless and timely advice to the Class of 2028
cards.access_notes: Open to all new students and faculty; typically held outdoors on the Historic Quad.

cards.title: First Meal at Commons
cards.subtitle: Central Dining Hub
cards.notes: Visit the 5-star rated dining hall for your first meal. Remember to sort your waste at the tray window and leave the black mugs inside.
cards.short_summary: The primary dining facility at Bates, known for its centralized 'one-dining-hall' culture.
cards.evidence_claim: The Commons is the main dining hall; weekend brunch and dinner are served until 8:00 PM or 8:30 PM depending on the day.
cards.source_title: Hours of Operation and Meal Prices | Dining, Conferences and Campus Events
cards.access_notes: Requires a Bates ID for entry on the student board plan. Open 7:00 AM to 9:00 PM on weekdays with varying weekend hours.

cards.title: Sunset at Mount David
cards.subtitle: Friday Evening Tradition
cards.notes: Take the short walk up the campus 'mountain' for a panoramic view of Lewiston and the White Mountains. It is a signature spot for first-weekend photos.
cards.short_summary: A rocky outcrop on campus that offers the best views of the surrounding area and is a popular student gathering spot.
cards.evidence_claim: Mount David is a campus landmark where catching a sunset is considered a first-year bucket list item.
cards.source_title: Tick All the Boxes: A Bucket List for Your First Year at Bates
cards.access_notes: Open 24/7; accessible via a short trail behind the Randall Student Center area.

cards.title: Chase Hall After Dark
cards.subtitle: Friday Night Social
cards.notes: Head to Chase Hall for C.H.A.D. events, which include craft nights, bingo, or live performances organized by Campus Activities & Traditions.
cards.short_summary: Weekly Friday night programming designed to provide inclusive, substance-free social options for students.
cards.evidence_claim: Campus Activities & Traditions (CAT) hosts weekly Friday night programming known as Chase Hall After Dark (C.H.A.D.).
cards.source_title: Campus Activities & Traditions (CAT) - Bates College
cards.access_notes: Events typically start in the evening; check Bates Engage for specific weekly times.

cards.title: Morning Walk at the Puddle
cards.subtitle: Saturday Morning Relaxation
cards.notes: Stroll around 'The Puddle.' While the famous Puddle Jump happens in winter, the lakeside path is a peaceful spot for a Saturday morning walk.
cards.short_summary: The central campus pond, affectionately known as 'The Puddle,' is the site of many Bates traditions.
cards.evidence_claim: Lake Andrews, known as the 'Puddle,' is a central campus feature and the site of the annual Puddle Jump tradition.
cards.source_title: Puddle Jump | 150 Years - Bates College
cards.access_notes: Outdoor area open 24/7 to the public.

cards.title: Explore the Museum of Art
cards.subtitle: Saturday Afternoon Culture
cards.notes: Visit the Olin Arts Center to see rotating exhibitions. It's a quiet, air-conditioned space to escape the move-in bustle.
cards.short_summary: A teaching museum that brings world-class art and ideas to the Bates campus and Lewiston community.
cards.evidence_claim: The Museum of Art is located in the Olin Arts Center and is open Saturdays from 10:00 AM to 5:00 PM.
cards.source_title: Visit | Museum of Art | Bates College
cards.access_notes: Open Monday-Saturday 10 AM - 5 PM; closed on Sundays.

cards.title: Late Night at the Den
cards.subtitle: Saturday Night Snack
cards.notes: Grab a burger or fries at this alternative dining spot in Chase Hall. It's the go-to place for late-night social interaction and food.
cards.short_summary: A popular retail dining and social space offering a more casual atmosphere than the main Commons.
cards.evidence_claim: The Bobcat Den in Chase Hall offers alternative dining and has recently reintroduced late-night hours.
cards.source_title: First Time in Four Years: Den Opens For Late-Night Option
cards.access_notes: Check current semester schedules for specific late-night hours; typically open until midnight on select nights.

cards.title: Find Your Study Nook
cards.subtitle: Sunday Afternoon Prep
cards.notes: Scope out the floors of Ladd Library to find your preferred study spot before classes start on Monday. The higher the floor, the quieter it gets.
cards.short_summary: The main research library at Bates, providing diverse study spaces and extensive academic resources.
cards.evidence_claim: Ladd Library is open on Sundays from 10:00 AM to 1:00 AM during the regular semester.
cards.source_title: Library Hours | Bates College
cards.access_notes: Bates ID required for access. Open until 1:00 AM on Sunday nights.

cards.title: AESOP Trip Departure
cards.subtitle: Sunday Evening Send-off
cards.notes: Gather on Alumni Walk to meet your student leaders for the Annual Entering Student Outdoor Program (AESOP). These trips are a core orientation experience.
cards.short_summary: A student-led outdoor orientation program that takes first-years on trips across Maine.
cards.evidence_claim: All first-year students participate in AESOP (Annual Entering Student Outdoor Program) during the orientation period.
cards.source_title: Residential Calendar | Residence Life - Bates College
cards.access_notes: Mandatory for first-year students; departure times vary by specific trip assignment.
